h1: Porcelain Veneers in Fort Worth, Texas
intro: Ultra-thin, custom-crafted porcelain shells that permanently transform your smile — correcting stains, chips, cracks, gaps, and misalignment simultaneously. The most versatile and dramatic cosmetic dental treatment available. Results that last 10–20 years.

sections.h2: What Are Porcelain Veneers & What Can They Fix?
body: Porcelain veneers are ultra-thin shells of dental porcelain — typically 0.5mm thick, about the same as a contact lens — that are custom-crafted to fit precisely over the front surface of your teeth. Once permanently bonded in place, they completely transform the appearance of your smile.

What makes veneers so powerful is their versatility. Unlike teeth whitening which only addresses discoloration, or bonding which repairs a single chip, a set of veneers can simultaneously correct multiple issues across all your front teeth — giving you a completely redesigned smile in just two or three visits.

Dr. Brown has over 30 years of experience designing veneer smiles. The result of his work looks completely natural — because great veneers require not just clinical skill, but an artistic eye for proportion, shade, and how teeth relate to your unique facial features.
bullets: Mimics the natural translucency of tooth enamel
Custom-designed for your face, skin tone & smile
Stain-resistant — stays brilliantly white long-term
Strong, durable and comfortable for everyday life

sections.h2: Types of Dental Veneers We Offer
body: Not all veneers are the same. Dr. Brown will recommend the best type for your specific teeth, goals, and budget during your consultation.

Traditional Porcelain Veneers — the gold standard in cosmetic dentistry. A thin layer of enamel is gently removed to create space for the veneer, which is then permanently bonded in place. Exceptional durability, stain resistance, and aesthetic quality — the best long-term investment. Lasts 10–20 years and is completed in 2–3 appointments.

Minimal-Prep Veneers — a more conservative approach that removes little to no enamel. This option is suitable for patients whose teeth have sufficient space to accommodate the veneer without any or minimal enamel removal — preserving more of the natural tooth structure.

Composite Resin Veneers — made from the same tooth-colored composite resin used for dental bonding. Applied and sculpted directly in-office in a single appointment — no laboratory required. A more affordable option, though less durable and stain-resistant than porcelain (lifespan 5–7 years typically).

sections.h2: How Your Porcelain Veneers Are Made & Placed
body: The veneer process is comfortable, predictable, and delivers results that exceed expectations. Here's exactly what to expect.

Consultation & Smile Design — Dr. Brown examines your teeth, takes photos and impressions, and discusses your smile goals in detail. Together you select the ideal veneer shade, shape, and size. In many cases, a digital smile preview is provided so you can visualise your result before committing.

Tooth Preparation & Impressions — a thin layer of enamel is gently removed from the front of each tooth under local anaesthesia. Precise impressions are sent to a master dental laboratory. Temporary veneers are placed so your smile looks great while your custom porcelain shells are being crafted.

Permanent Placement & Bonding — when your custom veneers arrive from the laboratory, you return to have them permanently bonded. Dr. Brown checks the fit, colour, and bite meticulously before final bonding. You leave with a completely transformed, stunning smile.

Master laboratory — only premium materials used
Customized to your face — proportion, shade & smile line
No rush — Dr. Brown personally oversees every detail
Natural results — nobody knows they're not your real teeth

sections.h2: Veneers vs. Other Cosmetic Dental Treatments
body: Understanding how veneers compare to whitening, bonding, and clear braces helps you choose the right treatment for your specific goals. Veneers fix multiple issues all at once — chips, cracks, gaps, staining, and minor misalignment — while whitening addresses discoloration only and bonding repairs one tooth at a time.
bullets: Longevity: veneers 10–20 years, bonding 5–8 years, whitening 1–3 years
Stain resistance: excellent for porcelain; teeth re-stain over time after whitening; moderate for bonding
Appointments: veneers 2–3, bonding 1, whitening 1 hour
Insurance: veneers and whitening usually not covered; bonding sometimes partially covered
Best for: multiple issues or a complete smile makeover

sections.h2: Are You a Good Candidate for Veneers?
body: Veneers may not be right if you have active tooth decay or gum disease (treat first), severely worn enamel with insufficient thickness, significant misalignment needing orthodontic treatment, severe teeth grinding (bruxism) without protection, or a very limited budget (bonding may be a better start). Dr. Brown will always recommend the most appropriate treatment for your situation — not just the most expensive one.
bullets: Your teeth are healthy with no active cavities or gum disease
You have sufficient enamel on the front of your teeth
You want to correct multiple cosmetic issues at once
You don't severely grind your teeth (or wear a night guard)
Your bite (occlusion) is reasonably healthy
You're committed to good oral hygiene after treatment

sections.h2: How to Make Your Veneers Last 10–20 Years
body: Porcelain veneers are remarkably durable — but caring for them properly will ensure they look beautiful for the full span of their lifespan. Here's Dr. Brown's complete aftercare guidance:
bullets: Use a soft-bristled brush and non-abrasive toothpaste; floss daily to keep gum tissue healthy around the veneer margins
Attend your bi-annual dental visits so Dr. Brown can check the condition of your veneers and bite regularly
Don't bite ice, pens, fingernails, or open packages with your teeth — porcelain can chip under extreme force
If you grind or clench your teeth at night, a custom night guard will protect your veneers from excessive wear
While porcelain is stain-resistant, the bonding cement at the margins can discolor — rinse after coffee, wine, or tea
Smoking significantly reduces the lifespan of veneers and affects the health of the surrounding gum tissue

faqs.a: Porcelain veneers are ultra-thin, custom-crafted shells of dental porcelain — typically about 0.5mm thick — that are permanently bonded to the front surfaces of your teeth. They completely transform the appearance of your smile by correcting staining, chips, cracks, gaps, minor misalignment, irregular shape, and uneven length all in a single comprehensive treatment. Unlike teeth whitening (which only addresses color) or dental bonding (which repairs one tooth at a time), a set of veneers redesigns your entire visible smile simultaneously — making them the most versatile and transformative cosmetic dental treatment available.

faqs.q: How long do porcelain veneers last?
faqs.a: With proper care, porcelain veneers typically last 10–20 years. They are highly durable, stain-resistant, and maintain their beautiful appearance for many years. To maximise lifespan: brush twice daily with a soft brush and non-abrasive toothpaste, attend bi-annual dental checkups so Dr. Brown can monitor your veneers, avoid biting hard objects like ice, pens, or fingernails, and wear a night guard if you grind your teeth while sleeping. When veneers do eventually need replacing after many years, the process is straightforward.

The veneer process is performed under effective local anaesthesia and the vast majority of patients experience little to no discomfort during the procedure. After the enamel preparation appointment, some temporary sensitivity is normal while wearing the temporary veneers — this is completely expected and resolves once the permanent veneers are placed. Once the permanent porcelain veneers are bonded in place, most patients report no pain whatsoever.

faqs.q: How many veneers do I need?
faqs.a: This depends entirely on your smile goals and which teeth are visible when you smile. Some patients choose a single veneer to address one specific problem tooth. Most smile makeovers involve 6–10 veneers covering the visible front teeth — typically all teeth you see when you give a full, natural smile. Dr. Brown will assess your smile during your consultation, take photographs, and carefully recommend the exact number of veneers needed to achieve a beautiful, balanced, and completely natural-looking result.

Traditional porcelain veneers are considered a permanent cosmetic treatment. Because a very thin layer of enamel (approximately 0.5mm) is removed to create space for the veneer, the tooth will always require a veneer or crown going forward. This is why the decision to get veneers should be made carefully and with full information. Minimal-prep and no-prep veneer options exist that remove little to no enamel, making them a more conservative and partially reversible choice. Dr. Brown will discuss all available options at your consultation — we never rush this decision.

Yes — high-quality porcelain veneers crafted and placed by an experienced cosmetic dentist are virtually indistinguishable from natural teeth. Porcelain uniquely mimics the translucency and light-reflecting properties of natural tooth enamel in a way that composite resin cannot replicate. Dr. Brown custom-designs the shade, shape, length, and texture of each veneer to complement your unique facial features, skin tone, lip line, and natural smile characteristics. The goal is always a result that looks like the best possible version of your own teeth — not an obviously "done" Hollywood smile.

faqs.q: How much do porcelain veneers cost in Fort Worth, TX?
faqs.a: The cost of porcelain veneers varies depending on the number of veneers needed, the complexity of your case, and the type of veneer chosen. Most dental insurance plans do not cover veneers as they are classified as a cosmetic procedure. We offer flexible financing through CareCredit — with low and 0% interest options — to make porcelain veneers accessible for a wider range of budgets. During your free consultation, Dr. Brown will provide a full, transparent cost estimate tailored to your specific treatment plan. There is never any obligation or pressure to proceed.

faqs.q: Can veneers fix crooked or misaligned teeth?
faqs.a: Veneers can address mild to moderate misalignment — giving the appearance of straighter, more evenly spaced teeth without orthodontic treatment. This approach is sometimes called "instant orthodontics" and is particularly popular with adult patients who want faster results. However, if your misalignment is significant — particularly if your bite (occlusion) is affected — Dr. Brown may recommend clear braces first, followed by veneers for the final cosmetic result. He will always recommend the most appropriate and conservative solution for your long-term dental health.
